# `public-declaration-docs`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: strict · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a public declaration on a module root's public surface without a doc
comment.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Public APIs need their caller-visible contract, error behavior, ownership, and
constraints documented near the declaration.

## When it fires

The strict profile is appropriate for libraries that treat their `pub`
declarations as supported API surface. Only declarations reachable from the
file's root through `pub` declarations count, including containers a `pub`
declaration selects with `if`, `orelse`, or `switch`, the types of fields, and
the containers a public type function returns. A `pub` member of a private
container, or of a container a private type function returns, cannot be
reached from any module root unless a `pub` alias in the file re-exports it
(`pub const Api = Impl;`, `pub const Small = Generic(8);`,
`pub const Handle = *Opaque;`, a `switch` branch, or a public type function's
`return Base(T);`). Names whose meaning a protocol fixes (`init`, `deinit`,
`hash`, `eql`, `format`, `Error`, `Options`, `std_options`, `main`) and the
`build` entry point need no comment, nor do the `std.json` hooks
`jsonStringify`, `jsonParse` and `jsonParseFromValue`. Test, fuzz and script
files publish no library API, so their `pub` declarations (fixtures shared
between test files, script helpers) are not reported. `build.zig` is, since
dependent build scripts import it, and so is a `testing/` directory, where
libraries publish testing helpers as `std.testing` does.

A constant whose value says what a comment would needs none: a literal
(`pub const max_len = 0x40;`, `pub const name: []const u8 = "x";`), an
aggregate of literals (`pub const empty: List = .{ .len = 0 };`), and an alias
or `@import` re-export (`pub const StaticBitSet = bit_set.StaticBitSet;`,
`pub const Thread = @import("Thread.zig");`), whose documentation is its
target's. An aggregate computed from calls or other declarations
(`pub const c_allocator: Allocator = .{ .vtable = &vtable, ... }`) still needs
one, since its value encodes a decision its name does not show. The entries of
a constant table, a namespace holding constants alone such as
`pub const SO = struct { pub const DEBUG = 1; ... };`, need no comment of their
own when they are computed with operators and casts (`1 << 4`, `IN | OUT`) and
the table is documented or holds only such entries; the table itself is
reported when it has no comment.

`zig-analyzer check` also reads the build scripts it scans. In a package whose
`build.zig` (with the files it imports) names the root file of every module it
exports with `b.addModule`, only those roots, the root modules of its
`b.addLibrary` artifacts, and what they re-export through `pub` declarations
count: `pub const a = @import("a.zig");` exposes `a.zig`, while
`pub const Api = @import("impl.zig").Api;` and
`const impl = @import("impl.zig"); pub const Api = impl.Api;` expose only `Api`
in `impl.zig`. A package that exports no module, an application, has no API to
document. Without such a build script, or when a module's root is not a literal
`b.path("...")`, and in the editor, each file is judged by its own surface.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
pub fn run() void {}
```
